mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5.0%, it signals labor market deterioration and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a contraction in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as corporate revenue expectations fall.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative 20-day returns in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock (INDPRO < 100), industrial production decline signals inflationary pressures and reduced economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO < 100, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening consumer demand and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: HOUST increases do not lead to positive 20-day returns in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation prompting monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days through higher consumer spending.
failure_condition: The joint increase in PAYEMS and decline in UNRATE does not produce positive 20-day returns in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During GDP contraction (GDPC1 growth < 0.5% annualized), economic slowdown fears drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days due to reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: In periods of GDPC1 growth < 0.5% annualized, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases.
